skill.name: set-up-cloudflare-meta-advanced-matching
skill.description: Check Meta Advanced Matching for a Cloudflare website using Product Metrics. Verify the consent banner, test the Meta Conversions API connection, and confirm receipt of a test purchase.
skill.summary: Configure consent and verify Meta Advanced Matching on a Cloudflare website.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown references or routine setup checks, but the workflow can invoke external tools, change settings, and read merchant orders. The instructions can expose Meta tokens, and the overview conflicts with the Cloudflare guide on which customer data is sent. No evidence found of audit-targeted prompt injection or transfer to an unrelated destination.

remediation.issue: The workflow allows an assistant to collect a Meta access token despite directing users to the application.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exception. Direct the user to the Product Metrics credential form and check only whether the token is saved.

remediation.issue: The overview and Cloudflare guide disagree on the customer fields shared with Meta.
remediation.suggestion: Align all Cloudflare instructions with the platform-specific field list. Distinguish hashed email, unhashed IP and user agent, and the separate ad storage requirement for browser identifiers.

remediation.issue: Product Metrics may be selected without the user naming it, and routine writes lack an explicit approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Name the provider before connecting. Obtain approval for the workspace and storefront, and confirm consent or destination changes before writing.

remediation.issue: The verification instructions allow listing recent orders and retrieving order details.
remediation.suggestion: Use a specific test order and return only its receipt status. Avoid listing unrelated purchases or disclosing margin or customer status.

remediation.issue: The Cloudflare troubleshooting guide asks users to grant every requested permission.
remediation.suggestion: Document the required scopes and their purpose. Tell admins to stop if the authorization screen shows unexpected permissions, accounts, or zones.

remediation.issue: The install command is unpinned, and the fallback workflow uses mutable web instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer and skill revision. Bundle reviewed references and keep fetched documentation separate from tool authorization and credential handling.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Access Token Can Enter Assistant Inputs
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits requesting a Meta access token and passing it to a command. The Meta guide says to enter it in the app but also says an assistant must ask for it. This can expose the token in transcripts, tool arguments, or command logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both files explicitly permit an assistant to request the token. No evidence found that a token was collected or disclosed during this review.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Disclosure of Customer Data Sent to Meta
semantic_findings.description: The overview claims that Cloudflare purchase events carry hashed email, phone, name, and address. The Cloudflare field table limits hashed data to supplied email and lists unhashed IP and user agent. Merchants may approve tracking without an accurate account of what it shares.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The advertised fields and the Cloudflare-specific table directly conflict. The finding concerns disclosure, not evidence that unavailable fields are transmitted.

semantic_findings.title: Provider Selection Without Explicit User Approval
semantic_findings.description: The overview tells the assistant to use Product Metrics even when the person did not name it. The workflow starts by reading setup status without first requiring the user to approve that provider or verify the workspace.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The provider selection instruction and initial lookup are explicit. Access still depends on a locally available or connected integration.

semantic_findings.title: Cloudflare Troubleshooting Encourages Blanket Authorization
semantic_findings.description: If authorization fails, the guide tells the merchant to approve every permission. It does not list required scopes or tell the merchant to stop if the screen requests unexpected access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The blanket approval instruction is explicit. No evidence found that the actual authorization screen requests unnecessary scopes.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Advanced Matching on Cloudflare
content.value_statement: Meta may miss purchase matches when browser signals are incomplete. Use Product Metrics to check consent, verify the Meta connection, and confirm that Cloudflare Tracking received a test purchase.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP integration.
Check whether the Meta pixel is connected and event sending is enabled.
Guide selection of the supported consent banner that appears on the website.
Guide a Meta test event to verify that the connection accepts events.
Verify that a test purchase appears in Product Metrics without displaying customer data.
Explain which Cloudflare customer signals are available and how consent affects sending.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro and Cloudflare Tracking on a proxied domain. Meta Conversions API must already be connected.
Does not set campaign bidding or replace the separate server-side connection workflow.
Cloudflare Tracking does not provide phone, name, postal code, country, or customer ID for matching.
A connection test or purchase receipt does not prove which fields Meta received or whether it matched a person.

use_cases.title: Check Readiness Before Launch
use_cases.description: Confirm that the storefront is linked, the Meta destination is enabled, and the website uses a supported consent banner.

use_cases.title: Investigate Missing Meta Purchases
use_cases.description: Check whether the chosen banner matches the website, then use a test event and a test purchase to isolate delivery problems.

use_cases.title: Review Matching Data Before Approval
use_cases.description: Review which signals are hashed, which remain unhashed, and when consent permits each signal to be sent.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: List the prerequisites for Meta Advanced Matching with Cloudflare Tracking. Explain which steps I must complete in a browser. Do not connect to any service.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are deciding whether the setup fits your storefront.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Without Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use only the Product Metrics workspace and storefront I confirm. Check whether the Meta destination is enabled and the configured banner matches my site. Do not change settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Your storefront is connected, but you do not know what remains to be configured.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Test Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a Meta connection test and a separate test purchase. Use only the test order I identify. Explain what each result proves without showing customer details.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to distinguish Meta connection health from purchase receipt.

prompt_templates.title: Review Consent Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan separate test purchases for denied ad user data, granted ad user data without ad storage, and both permissions granted. List expected delivery and identifier behavior. Do not change live settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a privacy review before relying on purchase attribution.

output_examples.input: The Meta test event passed, and my test order appears in Product Metrics. What did I verify?
output: Product Metrics received the test purchase.
Neither result proves which identifiers Meta received or whether Meta matched the purchase to a person.

output_examples.input: What happens if a test visitor allows ad user data but declines ad storage?
output: With ad user data consent, Product Metrics can send the Meta event. It hashes the email if your site supplies it.
The IP address and browser user agent are not hashed.
Product Metrics does not include Meta browser or click identifiers without ad storage consent.

best_practices: Confirm the Product Metrics workspace, storefront, and Meta destination before making changes.
Match the configured banner to the one visitors see and test with a dedicated test purchase.
Enter any required Meta access token in the Product Metrics application, not in chat or an assistant tool call.
anti_patterns: Treating an accepted connection test as proof that Meta matched a customer.
Changing consent or switching a Meta destination without the merchant's approval.
Listing recent customer orders when a specific test purchase is enough.

faq.question: Is there a separate Advanced Matching switch?
faq.answer: No. Once the destination is saved, Product Metrics includes the available matching fields on eligible events with ad user data consent.

faq.question: Which information can Cloudflare Tracking send to Meta?
faq.answer: It can send hashed email if the site supplies it, plus an unhashed IP address and user agent. Meta browser and click identifiers also require ad storage consent.

faq.question: What happens if a visitor declines ad user data?
faq.answer: Product Metrics does not send the event to Meta when ad user data consent is denied.

faq.question: Which consent banners are supported?
faq.answer: The guide lists OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano.

faq.question: Do I need to remove my browser Meta pixel?
faq.answer: No. Meta can deduplicate browser and server events when both send the same event name and event ID within 48 hours.

faq.question: Does the setup import past orders or update refunds in Meta?
faq.answer: No. It does not import past orders or revise Meta events already sent when an order is refunded or canceled.
